src: APPSC Group-II Prelims 2019
s: Which is the longest canal of commercial importance in Andhra?
x:
The Buckingham Canal is the longest navigation canal on the eastern coast of India and the most important canal of commercial significance in Andhra Pradesh. Constructed during the British period, the canal extends for about 796 km, running parallel to the Coromandel Coast from Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu. It connected several important ports and facilitated the transport of rice, salt, timber, textiles and agricultural produce before the development of railways and highways. In Andhra Pradesh, the canal connected important centres such as Kakinada, Eluru, Machilipatnam and Nellore, making it a vital route for inland water transport. Although the K.C. Canal, Bandar Canal and Eluru Canal are important irrigation canals, they do not possess the same commercial and navigational significance as the Buckingham Canal. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Longest Navigation Canal – Buckingham Canal
• Length – Approximately 796 km
• Importance – Inland navigation and commercial transport

The printed options did not include the correct answer (1935); it is added as option 5.
Tata's Karachi-Madras air mail began in 1932 via Bellary; from January 1935 it ran via Hyderabad, landing at Bolarum (the Hakimpet airfield). 1953 is impossible (Karachi was in Pakistan), and 1909-1919 precede the service.

s: Bhavanapadu Port is situated on the East Coast in between
x: Bhavanapadu (now Mulapeta) port is in Srikakulam district, north of Visakhapatnam, so it lies between Visakhapatnam and Paradeep. Kakinada and Machilipatnam are south of Visakhapatnam.
